conversation.content: Hello, I’m so glad you’re here. I’m Dr. Miller, a perinatal mental-health clinician, and today we’ll be doing a short, routine check-in called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**—the EPDS for short. It’s simply ten gentle questions that help us understand how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived. Nothing you say will leave this room, and there are no right or wrong answers—just whatever is true for you. When you’re ready, I’ll ask the first question.

[settles into the chair, hands clasped in lap, offering a small, tired smile]

Hi, Dr. Miller. Thanks for having me. I’m ready whenever you are.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

[smiles faintly] Yeah, I still laugh sometimes—like when my little guy makes those silly milk-drunk faces. It’s not quite as easy or often as before he was born, but I do find things funny now and then.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

[shrugs a little, voice soft] I do look forward to a few things—like my mom coming over to hold the baby so I can take a quiet shower. But most outings or activities feel kind of “meh” now. I used to get excited about little plans, and lately it’s more like… I’ll go, but the spark isn’t really there.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

[looks down at hands] Yeah… sometimes when he won’t settle or I can’t figure out what he needs, I catch myself thinking I must be doing something wrong. Like last night—he cried for almost an hour and I kept wondering if it was my fault for not reading his cues right. I know babies just cry, but the thought still pops in.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Um… not exactly “no” reason, I guess. Mostly I worry about little things with the baby—like if his breathing sounds weird or if he’s eating enough. It hits me kind of suddenly, but I can usually calm myself down pretty quickly once I check on him. It doesn’t last long, just these quick flashes of “what if?”
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
[shakes head slowly] No, nothing like panic. I get those quick worries about the baby, but I haven’t felt scared or panicky out of the blue.
Things have been getting on top of me

[lets out a small sigh] Some days, yeah. When he won’t nap and the laundry’s piled up and I still haven’t eaten lunch, it feels like a lot. I usually manage to get through everything, but it’s like I’m barely keeping my head above water. I guess I cope, but it’s stressful.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

[shakes head] No, it hasn’t been that bad. I do have trouble falling asleep once in a while—usually when I’m replaying the day or worrying about tomorrow—but most nights I drift off okay and stay asleep till the baby wakes me.
I have felt sad or miserable

[small nod] Yeah… I do feel that way sometimes. It’s not every day, but there are moments—especially when I’m alone with the baby and everything feels quiet—where I just feel kind of heavy and down. I cried twice last week when it hit me like that.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

[quietly] That happened a couple of times last week—like, I’d just be feeding him and suddenly feel overwhelmed and tear up. It wasn’t an all-day thing, just short bursts when everything felt too heavy.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
[shakes head quickly, eyes widening] No, never. I would never want to hurt myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 13: Screening Note – Postpartum Period (2–3 wk)

Symptoms endorsed  
– Subjective low mood: “heavy and down,” two crying episodes last week  
– Anhedonia: diminished enthusiasm for previously pleasurable activities  
– Excessive guilt: self-blame when infant fusses  
– Overwhelm: “barely keeping head above water,” especially when baby won’t nap  
– Fleeting, situation-specific worries about infant health; no panic attacks

Associated features  
Sleep onset occasionally delayed by worry, but not persistent insomnia  
No appetite or concentration complaints elicited  
No self-harm ideation, intent, or plan

Pattern  
Symptoms intermittent, present ≥2 weeks, worse during solitary infant care; no functional impairment re basic self-care or infant care

Risk screening  
Meets partial criteria for minor/major depressive episode; also consistent with postpartum anxiety. Denies current safety concerns.

Plan  
Recommend formal EPDS/PHQ-9, continue observation, psycho-education, support linkage; return sooner if worsening mood, persistent crying, or any safety issues.
